en: Petavatthu, Cūḷavagga 9. The Story of the Petas of the Fraudulent Judge [The Blessed One said: "Once upon a time, monks, there was a certain judge who was fraudulent and dishonest. He would take bribes and render unjust verdicts. After his death, he was reborn as a peta in the realm of ghosts. He appeared before the Blessed One, his body emaciated, his skin and flesh withered, his veins standing out like cords, and his form so terrifying that he inspired fear in all who saw him. With a voice choked with tears, he addressed the Blessed One: 'I am the one, Blessed One, who was a fraudulent judge in my previous life. I took bribes and rendered unjust verdicts. Because of that karma, I have been reborn here as a peta. I am constantly tormented by hunger and thirst; I find no relief anywhere. I wander from place to place, seeking food and drink, but I can never obtain it. Even when I see food or drink, it turns into fire or pus and blood as soon as I try to eat or drink it. May the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma so that I may find release from this state of suffering. Then the Blessed One, out of compassion for that peta, taught him the Dhamma. Having heard the Dhamma, the peta developed faith and passed away from that state to be reborn in a heavenly realm."
“You wear garlands, a crown, and armlets;
your limbs are anointed with sandalwood;
your facial complexion is serene.”
You shine like the color of the sun.
Your attendants are non-human beings who serve you.
Ten thousand maidens who were her attendants,
wearing shell-bracelets and golden armlets—
Adorned with a golden crest-jewel,
you are one of great majesty,
possessing a form that causes the hair to stand on end.
You yourself cut off the flesh from your own back and eat it.
What indeed [is the cause] of this in body or speech?
An evil deed was committed with the mind;
by the ripening of what karma are my own back-flesh [being eaten]?
“Do you eat [them] after plucking them yourself?
“I have acted for my own harm in this world of the living;”
Through slander, false speech,
and fraudulent deception—
having gone there into that assembly, I...
When the time for truth had arrived,
setting aside both benefit and the Dhamma,
I followed what was contrary to the Dhamma.
Thus does he who sells meat from his own back devour himself,
just as I devour him today.
"Your own back-flesh—
this was seen by you yourself, Nārada.
Those who are compassionate and skilled would say this."
Do not speak slander, nor do speak falsehood; do not be one who bites at the back.
Thus ends the ninth discourse on the hungry ghost of the fraudulent judge.
